findings.title: Finding places the denial in encounterable reality
findings.claim: The negated finding frames alteration as absent from what the addressee can encounter for the divine practice.
findings.mechanism: The imperfect finding verb governs the practice-domain and an explicit alteration object. With la negating the finding, the contact turns a bare statement of invariance toward the absence of any discoverable change, without making the verb mean metaphysical nonexistence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the denial from the addressee's position as finder, while keeping the object of that search clear.
findings.containment: The claim concerns what can be found or encountered in the stated domain; it does not establish a separate metaphysical theory of existence.

epistemic.reason: The support explicitly narrows the finding sense toward encounterability, while the source root display for this word is inconsistent with the QAC root and is not used to activate a branch.

findings.title: The addressee remains the finder
findings.claim: The imperfect second-person verb keeps the addressed Prophet grammatically present in the denial and allows its scope to extend beyond one moment.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the clause as addressed to a continuing finder, not as an impersonal description detached from the addressee.
findings.containment: This is an aspect and person effect of the focus verb, not a claim about an unlimited temporal duration beyond the clause.

epistemic.reason: QAC morphology and the trusted word analysis agree on the imperfect second-person form and its local attachment.

findings.title: Finding separates domain from object

findings.mechanism: Li governs sunnatina as a prepositional complement of tajidu, while the final accusative tahwilan is its direct object; the two complements therefore have different semantic roles.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish what the denial concerns from the thing denied as findable.
findings.containment: The finding verb remains ordinary; the case and attachment relations do the interpretive work.

epistemic.reason: The QAC alignment and attachment support independently preserve the prepositional domain and accusative object.

findings.containment: The ordering adds focus but does not turn the practice itself into the missing object.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus form and attachment evidence support the clitic placement and complement order.
